paper_metadata.title: A Low-Power Integrated Tuner for Cable Telephony Applications
paper_metadata.abstract: This paper describes an integrated tuner for cable telephony in a 0.35m, 27-GHz SOI BiCMOS technology. The IC integrates a complete dual-conversion signal path including upconverter, downconverter, variable-gain amplifier, LO synthesizers with fully integrated voltage-controlled oscillators, gain control circuitry, as well as digital calibration and interface circuits. It accepts signals in the 200–880-MHz band and produces a 44-MHz IF. Drawing 168 mA from a 3-V supply, the tuner system has a worst case noise factor of 7.3 dB, system phase noise below 78 dBc/Hz at a 10-kHz offset, spurs below 42 dBc for 137 5-dBmV input channels, a gain of 60 dB, and gain control range of 68 dB. The 13-mm2 IC meets specifications across an outdoor temperature range of 40 C to 100 C in production lots.

To circumvent the requirement for a front-end filter, this tuner design (Fig. 3) is based on a dual-conversion architecture in which the broad-band input first enters an upconverter which translates the desired channel to a 1.22-GHz IF.

The IC is tested in a module containing only the off-chip components shown in Fig. 3, as well as supply bypassing and a simple matching network preceding the upconverter to enhance the broad-band match.
